svg.aria-label: Bava Metzia 21b-22b categorized by Derech Tevunos chapter 9
svg.text: Bava Metzia 21b-22b — Despair that is not conscious
Not discussed in Derech Tevunos; labelled from the markers of ch. 9
57 sentences · indent shows what answers what · an arrow points at what the move acts on · a faded icon has been dealt with
Despair of recovering a lost item that is not a conscious feeling is not
considered despair: the owner keeps it, and the finder may not.
יאוש שלא מדעת, אביי אמר: לא הוי יאוש
accepted

text.tspan: undermines it, but leaves it possible

svg.text: And Rava said: it is considered despair, and the finder may keep it.
ורבא אמר: הוי יאוש
refuted
Where the item has a distinguishing mark, all agree it is not despair: when it
reached the finder's hand it reached it in a prohibited manner, since the owner
would say, I have a mark on it and will reclaim it.
בדבר שיש בו סימן — כולי עלמא לא פליגי דלא הוי יאוש
in doubt
An item swept off by the tide of the sea or by a flooding river the Merciful One
permits, even where it has a distinguishing mark, as we shall say below.
בזוטו של ים ובשלוליתו של נהר, אף על גב דאית ביה סימן, רחמנא שרייה

text.tspan: · פרוש מרוח · full explanation · inferred · ↑ acts on 2

svg.text: Where they disagree is over an item with no distinguishing mark. Abaye: he did
not know it fell. Rava: once he learns it fell he despairs, so he is held to
have despaired from the moment it fell.
כי פליגי בדבר שאין בו סימן
in doubt
A mnemonic for the series of proofs that follows: peh, mem, gimmel, shin; mem,
mem, kuf, gimmel, tet, yod; kaf, kaf, samekh, ayin, zayin.
(סימן פמג״ש ממקגט״י ככסע״ז)

text.tspan: objects to how it is put

svg.text: Come and hear: if one found scattered produce, it belongs to him. Why — is the
owner not unaware that it fell from him?
תא שמע: פירות מפוזרין, הא לא ידע דנפל מיניה!
answered
תא שמע

text.tspan: · ישוב · settlement · Rav Ukva bar Ḥama · inferred

svg.text: Did Rav Ukva bar Ḥama not say: we are dealing with kernels left during the
gathering on the threshing floor? That is a deliberate loss, so the despair is
conscious.
הא אמר רב עוקבא בר חמא: הכא במכנשתא דבי דרי עסקינן, דאבידה מדעת היא
הכא במאי עסקינן

text.tspan: objects to how it is put

svg.text: Come and hear: if one found scattered coins, these belong to him. Why — is the
owner not unaware that they fell from him?
תא שמע: מעות מפוזרות — הרי אלו שלו. אמאי? הא לא ידע דנפל מיניה!
answered
תא שמע
There too it is as R. Yitzḥak said: a person is prone to feel his money pouch
constantly, so he learns of the loss almost at once.
התם נמי כדרבי יצחק דאמר: אדם עשוי למשמש בכיסו בכל שעה ושעה

text.tspan: objects to how it is put

svg.text: Come and hear: if one found round cakes of pressed figs or baker's loaves, these
belong to him. Why — is the owner not unaware that they fell from him?
תא שמע: עיגולי דבילה וככרות של נחתום — הרי אלו שלו. אמאי? והא לא ידע דנפל מיניה?
answered
תא שמע
There too: since they are heavy, he knows they fell.
התם נמי, אגב דיקירי מידע ידע בהו

text.tspan: objects to how it is put

svg.text: Come and hear: and strips of purple wool, these belong to him. And why — is the
owner not unaware that they fell from him?
תא שמע: ולשונות של ארגמן — הרי אלו שלו. ואמאי? הא לא ידע דנפל מיניה!
answered
תא שמע
There too: since they are valuable he keeps feeling for them, as R. Yitzḥak said
of coins.
התם נמי, אגב דחשיבי משמושי ממשמש בהו, וכדרבי יצחק

text.tspan: objects to how it is put

svg.text: Come and hear: one who finds coins in synagogues, in study halls, and anywhere
the multitudes are found — these belong to him, because the owners despair of
them. And is the owner not unaware that they fell?
תא שמע: המוצא מעות בבתי כנסיות ובבתי מדרשות … הרי אלו שלו, מפני שהבעלים מתיאשין…
answered
תא שמע
R. Yitzḥak says: a person is prone to feel his money pouch constantly.
אמר רבי יצחק: אדם עשוי למשמש בכיסו בכל שעה

text.tspan: objects to how it is put

svg.text: Come and hear: from when may anyone collect gleanings? Once the nemushot have
passed through the field. Why — granted the poor here despair, there are poor
elsewhere who know nothing of it and do not despair.
תא שמע: מאימתי כל אדם מותרים בלקט? משילכו בה הנמושות … נהי דעניים דהכא מיאשי, א…
answered
תא שמע
They say: since there are poor people here, those elsewhere despaired from the
outset, saying, the poor who are there will gather it.
אמרי: כיון דאיכא עניים הכא, הנך מעיקרא איאושי מיאש

text.tspan: objects to how it is put

svg.text: Come and hear: dried figs found on the path, and figs found beneath a fig tree
overhanging a path, are permitted and not robbery. Why — is the owner not
unaware?
תא שמע: קציעות בדרך … וכן תאנה הנוטה לדרך ומצא תאנים תחתיה — מותרות משום גזל
answered
תא שמע
Granted, the first clause is not difficult for Abaye: dried figs are valuable,
so he feels for them; and of a fig tree one knows that its fruit falls.
בשלמא רישא לאביי לא קשיא: אגב דחשיבי — ממשמש בהו. תאנה נמי מידע ידיע דנתרא

text.tspan: objects to how it is put

svg.text: But the latter clause is difficult for Rava, which teaches: in the case of
olives or carobs it is prohibited.
אלא סיפא לרבא קשיא, דקתני ״בזיתים ובחרובים אסור״
answered
R. Abbahu said: an olive is different, since its appearance proves whose it is;
the finder knows an olive tree standing in a man's place belongs to that man.
אמר רבי אבהו: שאני זית, הואיל וחזותו מוכיח עליו
stands

text.tspan: objects to how it is put

svg.text: If so, the first clause should be prohibited as well.
אי הכי, אפילו רישא נמי!
answered
אי הכי
Rav Pappa said: a fig becomes disgusting with its fall, so the owner does not
want it and renounces ownership.
אמר רב פפא: תאנה עם נפילתה נמאסת

text.tspan: objects to how it is put

svg.text: Come and hear: a thief who took from this one and gave to that one, and likewise
a robber, and likewise the Jordan — what he took he took and what he gave he
gave; the recipient need not return it.
תא שמע: הגנב שנטל מזה ונתן לזה … מה שנטל נטל ומה שנתן נתן
answered
תא שמע
Granted for the robber and the Jordan, whom the owner sees and so despairs; but
a thief — does the owner see him, that he should despair?
בשלמא גזלן וירדן, דקא חזי להו ומיאש. אלא גנב, מי קא חזי ליה דמיאש?
Rav Pappa interpreted the thief of the baraita as an armed bandit, so the owner
does know and does despair.
תרגמה רב פפא בלסטים מזוין
stands

text.tspan: objects to how it is put

svg.text: If so, this is the same as a robber — why mention two identical cases?
אי הכי היינו גזלן!
answered
הינו הך
The baraita mentioned two types of robber; in both the owner knew his item had
been taken.
תרי גווני גזלן

text.tspan: objects to how it is put

svg.text: Come and hear: if a river swept away one's beams, wood or stones and set them in
another's field, they are the field-owner's, because the owners despaired. The
reason is that they despaired — but unspecified, they would not be his.
תא שמע: שטף נהר קוריו, עציו, ואבניו … מפני שנתיאשו הבעלים. טעמא דנתיאשו הבעלים,…
weakened
תא שמע
With what are we dealing here? A case where the owners were able to rescue them,
so declining to do so shows despair.
הכא במאי עסקינן? כשיכול להציל
weakened
הכא במאי עסקינן

text.tspan: objects to how it is put

svg.text: If so, say the latter clause: if the owners were pursuing them, he must return
them. If they could rescue them, why specifically pursuing? Even not pursuing
they should remain his.
אי הכי אימא סיפא: אם היו הבעלים מרדפין אחריהם — חייב להחזיר. אי ביכולין להציל, …
weakened
אי הכי

text.tspan: offers a way out, without claiming it is true

svg.text: With what are we dealing? A case where they could rescue them only with
difficulty: pursuing shows they did not despair, not pursuing shows they did.
הכא במאי עסקינן? ביכולין להציל על ידי הדחק
הכא במאי עסקינן

text.tspan: objects to how it is put

svg.text: Come and hear: one who separated teruma from another's field without permission
— if the owner came and said, you should have taken from the better ones, and
better ones are found, his teruma is teruma. Why? At the time he separated, he
did not know.
תא שמע: … אם נמצאו יפות מהן — תרומתו תרומה. אמאי? בעידנא דתרם הא לא הוה ידע!
answered
תא שמע
Rava interpreted the matter in accordance with Abaye: it is a case where the
owner had already appointed him as an agent.
תרגמה רבא אליבא דאביי: דשוייה שליח
stands
So too it stands to reason: were he not an agent, would his teruma be teruma?
The verse says "you also", including your agent — as you act knowingly, so your
agent acts knowingly.
הכי נמי מסתברא … והא ״אתם״ ״גם אתם״ אמר רחמנא לרבות שלוחכם
תניא כותה ד

text.tspan: objects to how it is put

svg.text: But if he was simply an agent, the teruma should be valid whatever the owner
later said; why should finding better produce decide it?
אי הכי, מאי נפקא מינה ב״כלך אצל יפות״?
answered
Rather: he made him an agent and said go and separate, without saying separate
from these. An unspecified instruction means the middling; he went and took from
the best, and the owner said, you should have gone to the better ones.
אלא הכא במאי עסקינן — כגון דשוייה שליח, ואמר ליה ״זיל תרום״, ולא אמר ליה ״תרום …
stands
הכא במאי עסקינן
Ameimar, Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi came to the orchard of Mari bar Isak. His
sharecropper set dates and pomegranates before them; Ameimar and Rav Ashi ate,
Mar Zutra did not. Mari bar Isak arrived and said to the sharecropper: why did
you not bring the Sages from those finer ones?
אמימר ומר זוטרא ורב אשי אקלעו לבוסתנא דמרי בר איסק …
accepted
כך היה מנהגו של

text.tspan: objects to how it is put

svg.text: Ameimar and Rav Ashi said to Mar Zutra: now why is the Master not eating? Is it
not taught that if better ones are found, his teruma is teruma?
אמרו ליה אמימר ורב אשי למר זוטרא: השתא אמאי לא אכיל מר? והתניא: אם נמצאו יפות מ…
answered
He said to them, thus said Rava: they said "you should have gone to the better
ones" only regarding teruma, because it is a mitzva and he is content; but here
he spoke only out of embarrassment.
אמר להו, הכי אמר רבא: לא אמרו ״כלך אצל יפות״ אלא לענין תרומה בלבד … אבל הכא — מ…

text.tspan: objects to how it is put

svg.text: Come and hear: if the dew is still on the produce and he was glad, it is within
"when water is placed"; if it had dried, even though he was glad, it is not. Is
the reason not that we do not say, since he is content now he was content from
the start?
תא שמע: עודהו הטל עליהן ושמח — הרי זה בכי יותן. נגבו, אף על פי ששמח — אינן בכי …
answered
תא שמע
It is different there, for although it is read "when it is placed", it is
written "when one places" — not until he places it.
שאני התם, דכתיב ״כי יתן״ — עד שיתן
stands

text.tspan: objects to how it is put

svg.text: If so, the first clause too should not render it susceptible, since the dew fell
and was not placed by the owner.
אי הכי, רישא נמי!
answered
ולפלג … ברישא!
There, it is as Rav Pappa explained.
התם כדרב פפא
stands

text.tspan: · רמיא · apparent contradiction · Rav Pappa · inferred

svg.text: For Rav Pappa raised a contradiction: it is written "when one places", and we
read it "when it is placed". How so?
דרב פפא רמי, כתיב ״כי יתן״, וקרינן ״כי יותן״! הא כיצד?
answered
… רמי, כתיב … וכתיב
We require "when it is placed" to resemble "when one places": just as placing is
with his knowledge, so being placed must be with his knowledge.
בעינן ״כי יותן״ דומיא ד״כי יתן״: מה ״יתן״ לדעת, אף ״כי יותן״ נמי לדעת

text.tspan: objects to how it is put
· פרכא · objection · R. Yoḥanan · inferred · ↑ acts on 2

svg.text: Come and hear what R. Yoḥanan said in the name of R. Yishmael ben Yehotzadak:
from where do we know that an item swept off by a river is permitted? "Which
shall be lost from him, and you have found it" — that which is lost to him but
available to any man; excluding this, which is lost to him and available to no
one.
תא שמע דאמר רבי יוחנן משום רבי ישמעאל בן יהוצדק: מנין לאבידה ששטפה נהר שהיא מות…
תא שמע

text.tspan: · סתירה · direct contradiction · inferred · ↑ acts on 2

svg.text: And the prohibition resembles the permission: just as the permission holds
whether or not there is a distinguishing mark, so the prohibition holds whether
or not there is one — until it is known that the owner despaired.
ואיסורא דומיא דהיתירא: מה היתירא בין דאית בה סימן ובין דלית בה סימן — שריא, אף …

text.tspan: · תיובתא · refutation · inferred · undefined in source · ↑ acts on 2

svg.text: The refutation of Rava is indeed a conclusive refutation.
תיובתא דרבא, תיובתא!
And the halakha is in accordance with Abaye in the disputes represented by the
mnemonic yod, ayin, lamed; kuf, gimmel, mem.
והלכתא כוותיה דאביי ביע״ל קג״ם
stands

text.tspan: · שאלה · query · Rav Aḥa b. Rava · inferred

svg.text: Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi: now that Rava has been refuted, how do
we eat dates blown down by the wind?
אמר ליה רב אחא בריה דרבא לרב אשי: וכי מאחר דאיתותב רבא — הני תמרי דזיקא היכי אכ…
answered
He said to him: since there are creeping things that eat them once they fall,
the owner despairs of them from the outset.
אמר ליה: כיון דאיכא שקצים ורמשים דקא אכלי להו, מעיקרא יאושי מיאש מנייהו
stands

text.tspan: · שאלה · query · Rav Aḥa b. Rava · inferred

svg.text: And orphans, who are not capable of relinquishing property and so cannot despair
— what then?
יתמי דלאו בני מחילה נינהו, מאי?
answered
He said to him: we do not presume a valley to be land belonging to orphans.
אמר ליה: באגא בארעא דיתמי לא מחזקינן
stands

text.tspan: asks which of two ways the law goes
· אבעיא · question of principle · Rav Aḥa b. Rava · inferred

svg.text: Where their ownership is already established, what is the law? And where the
trees are walled about, what is the law?
מוחזק ועומד, מאי? כרכתא, מאי?
answered
בעא מנה … מהו? … או … אזלינן
He said to him: they are forbidden.
אמר ליה: אסירן
פשט … ד
